title: Everything went silent… but heaven was not still.
paragraphs: Everything went silent… but heaven was not still.

Black Saturday.
Luke 23:56 says they rested… according to the commandment.
Rested?

After nails tore flesh.
After breath gave out.
After hope looked buried behind a stone.
They rested.

But don’t mistake silence for absence.
Don’t confuse stillness with defeat.

Because while earth held its breath…
God was still writing.

The disciples were shattered.
Dreams crushed.
Promises felt broken.

The women who loved Him?
They prepared spices… but paused.
Obedient even in grief.

That’s the tension of Black Saturday:
Faith… with no visible answer.

No miracles.
No voice from heaven.
No movement.
Just waiting.
But here’s what we miss…

The grave was not a period.
It was a comma.

Jesus didn’t lose.
He entered the silence on purpose.

Some scholars interpret that this was the day Christ descended, proclaiming victory even in the realm of death (see 1 Peter 3:19). Whether fully understood or not—this was not inactivity. This was invasion.

Hell thought it had Him.
Death thought it won.
But heaven was counting down.
And maybe that’s where you are.

In between.
Between prayer and answer.
Between promise and fulfillment.
Your “Black Saturday.”

Nothing moving.
Nothing changing.
Everything quiet.
Listen to me.
God does His deepest work in the dark.

Seeds grow underground.
Wombs carry life in hidden places.
And graves…
Don’t stay full when Jesus is involved.

So if you’re in the silence right now—
don’t walk away.

Rest… even when you don’t understand.
Trust… even when you can’t see.
Because Sunday is coming.
Resurrection is already in motion.
